{{short description|Israeli-American statistician (1918–2004)}}
'''Benjamin Epstein''' (March 5, 1918 – December 22, 2004)<ref>{{Cite web |title=Scientific Legacy Database |website=Institute of Mathematical Statistics  |url=https://imstat.org/scientific-legacy-database/ |language=en}}</ref> was an Israeli-American statistician and a pioneer in statistical theory of reliability. He and [[Milton Sobel]] are credited with introducing the statistical framework for life testing while working together at [[Wayne State University]] as faculty members during the 1950s.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Mukhopadhyay |first=Nitis |date=2000 |title=A conversation with Milton Sobel |url=https://projecteuclid.org/journals/statistical-science/volume-15/issue-2/A-conversation-with-Milton-Sobel/10.1214/ss/1009212756.full |journal=Statistical Science |volume=15 |issue=2 |doi=10.1214/ss/1009212756 |issn=0883-4237}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book |last=Grosh |first=Doris Lloyd |url=https://www.google.com/books/edition/A_Primer_of_Reliability_Theory/JeubAAAACAAJ?hl=en |title=A Primer of Reliability Theory |date=1989 |publisher=Wiley |isbn=978-0-471-50353-8 |language=en}}</ref>

== Education and career ==
Epstein was born in [[Boston]], [[Massachusetts]], and went to study at the [[Boston Latin School]].<ref name=ims></ref> He entered [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]] to study mathematics at the age of 16 and went on to obtain an [[Bachelor of Science|S.B.]] in 1937 and an M.Sc. in 1938, both in mathematics. He received his PhD in mathematics at [[University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign]] on [[transform theory]] in 1941 under the supervision of David G. Bourgin.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Berg |first=Menachem |last2=Epstein |first2=Benjamin |date=1978 |title=Comparison of Age, Block, and Failure Replacement Policies |url=http://ieeexplore.ieee.org/document/5220230/ |journal=IEEE Transactions on Reliability |volume=R-27 |issue=1 |pages=25–29 |doi=10.1109/TR.1978.5220230 |issn=0018-9529|url-access=subscription }}</ref> During World War II, Epstein worked as an applied mathematician to investigate [[quality control]] problems, first at the [[Frankford Arsenal]] and then at [[Westinghouse Electric Corporation]] in [[Pittsburgh]].<ref name=ims>{{Cite web |last=Adler |first=Robert |last2=Weissman |first2=Ishay |date=2005 |title=Obituary: Benjamin Epstein (1918-2004) |url=https://imstat.org/wp-content/uploads/Bulletin34_8.pdf |website=IMS Bulletin}}</ref>

After the war, Epstein joined the Coal Research Laboratory at [[Carnegie Institute of Technology]] in 1946 and also worked as a lecturer at the Department of Mathematics at the university.<ref>{{Cite journal |date=1946 |title=News and Notices |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/2305520 |journal=The American Mathematical Monthly |volume=53 |issue=6 |pages=347–350 |issn=0002-9890}}</ref> Epstein joined the mathematics department at [[Wayne State University]] in 1948, where he was later joined by [[Milton Sobel]] for work on [[reliability theory]] and life testing. He stayed at [[Wayne State University]] until 1960 when he became a full professor. Epstein moved to [[Stanford University]] in 1960, where he was a professor of statistics for a few years before becoming an industry consultant in the [[Palo Alto, California|Palo Alto]] area. Epstein relocated to Israel in 1968 to found the statistics group at [[Technion – Israel Institute of Technology|Technion]] in the Industrial Engineering and Management department. He became the first full professor in statistics at Technion and taught there until his retirement in 1986.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Epstein, Benjamin |url=https://dds.technion.ac.il/people/in-memoriam/benjamin-epstein/ |website=The Faculty of Data and Decision Sciences |language=en-US}}</ref><ref name=ims></ref>

== Honors and awards ==
In 1957, Epstein became a Fellow of the [[American Statistical Association]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=American Statistical Association |url=https://ww2.amstat.org/fellows/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251118080556/https://ww2.amstat.org/fellows/ |archive-date=2025-11-18 |website=American Statistical Association}}</ref> He was elected a fellow of the [[Institute of Mathematical Statistics]] in 1958. Epstein was a founding member of the Israeli Statistical Association (now Israel Statistics and Data Science Association) and was the president from 1979 to 1981. In 1974, he received the [[Shewhart Medal]] from the [[American Society for Quality]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Shewhart Medalists {{!}} ASQ |url=https://asq.org/about-asq/asq-awards/honors/shewhart?srslt |website=asq.org}}</ref>
